scope: Thirty-two finite molecular models grouped into twelve partial1.25 family lessons; named contexts and selected reagents remain distinct. No full collection, practical trial or activated exam template.

models.conditions: Cold-water school model; state of metal describes initial sample.
models.limits: No uniform air-tarnish equation inferred; comparison is supervised context, no practical trial.
models.wordEquation: lithium + water → lithium hydroxide + hydrogen

models.conditions: Cold-water school model; state of metal describes initial sample.
models.limits: No uniform air-tarnish equation inferred; comparison is supervised context, no practical trial.
models.wordEquation: sodium + water → sodium hydroxide + hydrogen

models.conditions: Cold-water school model; state of metal describes initial sample.
models.limits: No uniform air-tarnish equation inferred; comparison is supervised context, no practical trial.
models.wordEquation: potassium + water → potassium hydroxide + hydrogen

models.conditions: Dilute aqueous displacement model; product concentration chosen within solubility.
models.limits: Na+ spectator is editorial choice. Iodine can precipitate or form other dissolved species at other concentrations; do not transfer room-temperature pure-element states. Reverse displacement unsupported.
models.wordEquation: chlorine + sodium bromide → sodium chloride + bromine

models.conditions: Dilute aqueous displacement model; product concentration chosen within solubility.
models.limits: Na+ spectator is editorial choice. Iodine can precipitate or form other dissolved species at other concentrations; do not transfer room-temperature pure-element states. Reverse displacement unsupported.
models.wordEquation: chlorine + sodium iodide → sodium chloride + iodine

models.conditions: Dilute aqueous displacement model; product concentration chosen within solubility.
models.limits: Na+ spectator is editorial choice. Iodine can precipitate or form other dissolved species at other concentrations; do not transfer room-temperature pure-element states. Reverse displacement unsupported.
models.wordEquation: bromine + sodium iodide → sodium bromide + iodine

models.conditions: Burning hydrogen; hot product region.
models.limits: Condensation later yields liquid water; same model supports pop test without a duplicate entry.
models.wordEquation: hydrogen + oxygen → water

models.conditions: Ignited sulfur in oxygen; atomic S school representation.
models.limits: If S8 supplied use S8 + 8O2 → 8SO2; not another required case.
models.wordEquation: sulfur + oxygen → sulfur dioxide

models.conditions: Heating specified pure-CuCO3 model.
models.limits: Basic copper carbonate differs: supplied CuCO3·Cu(OH)2 gives 2CuO + CO2 + H2O; not silently interchangeable.
models.wordEquation: copper(II) carbonate → copper(II) oxide + carbon dioxide

models.conditions: Heated magnesium and steam.
models.limits: Cold-water reaction is very slow and gives hydroxide; not universal water product.
models.wordEquation: magnesium + water → magnesium oxide + hydrogen

models.conditions: Dilute hydrochloric acid.
models.limits: Mg/Zn/Fe in 2.21 are examples, not exclusive mandatory cases.
models.wordEquation: magnesium + hydrochloric acid → magnesium chloride + hydrogen

models.conditions: Dilute sulfuric acid, suitable exposed iron surface.
models.limits: Iron(II), not iron(III); concentrated/oxidising-acid behaviour not represented. This and preceding case cover both practical acid types without six compulsory combinations.
models.wordEquation: iron + sulfuric acid → iron(II) sulfate + hydrogen

models.conditions: Explicit heated solid-oxide reduction stage below iron melting point.
models.limits: Carbon supplies reducing CO in conventional extraction; later furnace melting not modelled. Do not claim iron(s) throughout furnace or mandate every furnace equation.
models.wordEquation: iron(III) oxide + carbon monoxide → iron + carbon dioxide

models.conditions: Warm dilute acid, excess oxide filtered off; concentrate filtrate and cool.
models.limits: Crystallisation gives hydrated CuSO4·5H2O, not directly anhydrous solid from this aqueous equation. Shared preparation context avoids duplicate equation.
models.wordEquation: copper(II) oxide + sulfuric acid → copper(II) sulfate + water

models.conditions: Mix suitable soluble solutions; filter, wash, dry under supervised procedure.
models.limits: Nitrate and sodium sulfate are choices, not the sole prescribed reagents. Net Pb2+ + SO4^2− → PbSO4.
models.wordEquation: lead(II) nitrate + sodium sulfate → lead(II) sulfate + sodium nitrate

models.conditions: Carbon dioxide feed into limewater; initial cloudy precipitate.
models.limits: Excess CO2 can clear cloudiness; further hydrogencarbonate model is not a new compulsory bank case.
models.wordEquation: carbon dioxide + calcium hydroxide → calcium carbonate + water

models.conditions: Warm ammonium solution with sodium hydroxide; identify evolved NH3 using damp red litmus.
models.limits: NH4Cl choice representative; net NH4+ + OH− → NH3 + H2O. Not hypothetical NH4OH isolated product.
models.wordEquation: ammonium chloride + sodium hydroxide → ammonia + sodium chloride + water

models.conditions: Aqueous sodium hydroxide gives the named precipitate.
models.limits: Chloride is representative soluble source. CuII blue, FeII green, FeIII brown; net ion charge balance zero. FeII precipitate can oxidise on standing.
models.wordEquation: copper(II) chloride + sodium hydroxide → copper(II) hydroxide + sodium chloride

models.conditions: Aqueous sodium hydroxide gives the named precipitate.
models.limits: Chloride is representative soluble source. CuII blue, FeII green, FeIII brown; net ion charge balance zero. FeII precipitate can oxidise on standing.
models.wordEquation: iron(II) chloride + sodium hydroxide → iron(II) hydroxide + sodium chloride

models.conditions: Aqueous sodium hydroxide gives the named precipitate.
models.limits: Chloride is representative soluble source. CuII blue, FeII green, FeIII brown; net ion charge balance zero. FeII precipitate can oxidise on standing.
models.wordEquation: iron(III) chloride + sodium hydroxide → iron(III) hydroxide + sodium chloride

models.conditions: Acidify sample with dilute nitric acid, then add silver nitrate.
models.limits: Never acidify with HCl; Na+ spectator choice not mandatory. AgCl white, AgBr cream, AgI yellow; net Ag+ + X− → AgX.
models.wordEquation: silver nitrate + sodium chloride → silver chloride + sodium nitrate

models.conditions: Acidify sample with dilute nitric acid, then add silver nitrate.
models.limits: Never acidify with HCl; Na+ spectator choice not mandatory. AgCl white, AgBr cream, AgI yellow; net Ag+ + X− → AgX.
models.wordEquation: silver nitrate + sodium bromide → silver bromide + sodium nitrate

models.conditions: Acidify sample with dilute nitric acid, then add silver nitrate.
models.limits: Never acidify with HCl; Na+ spectator choice not mandatory. AgCl white, AgBr cream, AgI yellow; net Ag+ + X− → AgX.
models.wordEquation: silver nitrate + sodium iodide → silver iodide + sodium nitrate

models.conditions: Acidify separate aqueous sample with dilute HCl then add BaCl2.
models.limits: Not sulfuric acid acidification; white precipitate. Na+ source representative; net Ba2+ + SO4^2− → BaSO4.
models.wordEquation: barium chloride + sodium sulfate → barium sulfate + sodium chloride

models.conditions: Idealised hot molten-electrolyte overall process with carbon anodes; alumina is dissolved in the cryolite bath. The (l) shorthand denotes its molten-electrolyte context, not an assertion of pure liquid alumina.
models.limits: Carbon anodes are consumed in this CO2-only overall model. Do not combine consumed carbon with oxygen as the sole final anode gas. An inert-anode model has a different overall equation; actual process gases can be mixed.
models.wordEquation: aluminium oxide + carbon → aluminium + carbon dioxide

models.conditions: Supervised oxygen-removal illustration with white phosphorus represented as P4. State labels refer to the initial solid sample and subsequently cooled collected solid oxide, rather than all phases at the flame.
models.limits: Iron and phosphorus are publisher examples, not the only permitted substances. Hot oxide vapour must cool and products must be removed/absorbed as appropriate before interpreting gas volume; not an unsupervised procedure. P2O5 is the empirical formula, not another atom-balanced P4 product with coefficient one.
models.wordEquation: phosphorus + oxygen → phosphorus(V) oxide

models.conditions: Selected heated displacement model using supplied solid reactants and cooled solid products; appropriate initiation is needed in a supervised demonstration.
models.limits: Magnesium gains oxygen and is oxidised; copper(II) oxide loses oxygen and is reduced. State labels are not a claim that every material remains solid at every instant of a vigorous hot reaction.
models.wordEquation: magnesium + copper(II) oxide → magnesium oxide + copper

models.conditions: Dilute aqueous sulfuric acid fully neutralised by the stoichiometric amount of aqueous sodium hydroxide; sodium sulfate remains dissolved.
models.limits: Two hydroxide equivalents per sulfuric acid are required for this normal sulfate product. Partial neutralisation can give a different salt; the complete equation is not a claim about every mixing ratio.
models.wordEquation: sulfuric acid + sodium hydroxide → sodium sulfate + water

models.conditions: Dilute nitric acid reacts with the solid hydroxide base; the magnesium nitrate product remains in dilute solution.
models.limits: This is an acid/base model, not a nitric-acid/metal hydrogen prediction. One Mg2+ requires two nitrate ions; both hydroxide groups form water.
models.wordEquation: magnesium hydroxide + nitric acid → magnesium nitrate + water

models.conditions: Aqueous ammonia accepts a proton from dilute hydrochloric acid; the resulting ammonium salt stays dissolved.
models.limits: A base need not contain an OH group. This is different from the cool gas-recombination NH3/HCl demonstration forming solid ammonium chloride; do not copy (s) from that other context.
models.wordEquation: ammonia + hydrochloric acid → ammonium chloride

models.conditions: Dilute nitric acid reacts with magnesium carbonate; nitrate stays dissolved.
models.limits: Carbonate gives CO2 and water, not hydrogen. The chosen acid/carbonate pair is a family illustration, not an extra prescribed named practical.
models.wordEquation: magnesium carbonate + nitric acid → magnesium nitrate + water + carbon dioxide

models.conditions: Dilute sulfuric acid reacts with magnesium carbonate; magnesium sulfate remains in dilute solution.
models.limits: This selected soluble-product case is not a universal claim that every carbonate reacts fully with every acid. An insoluble surface product can inhibit other combinations.
models.wordEquation: magnesium carbonate + sulfuric acid → magnesium sulfate + water + carbon dioxide

remainingBoundaries: Rust has no fabricated fixed hydration formula; existing variable-composition teaching remains applicable.
Calcium/cold-water optional family example needs a deliberately chosen dissolved/precipitated hydroxide context; not every reagent combination is compulsory.
Aluminium cathode/charge half-equation is separate supporting evidence, not a full overall molecule model.
Reconcile all remaining source families, polymer representations and unfamiliar supplied-reaction tasks before any1.25 completion decision.
